observations: Three photos show a large office machine wrapped in clear plastic, likely a photocopier or laser printer.
The machine has a beige or off-white casing with visible branding and model text.
The machine is stacked on top of other similar units, suggesting bulk or resale.
The plastic wrap is crinkled and shows signs of handling or storage.
No power cord, paper tray, or control panel is visible in any photo.
The machine appears to be new or unused, as it is still wrapped.

claims.claim: The AR-M207 is packed with an extensive range of superb performance functions
claims.evidence: No photo shows the machine's control panel, paper tray, or any interface. The claim about 'superb performance functions' cannot be verified from the photos alone.

risks.risk: The machine may be non-functional or have internal damage not visible in photos.
risks.proof: A video showing the machine powering on, printing a test page, and operating the control panel.

risks.risk: The machine may be missing essential components such as the power cord, paper tray, or toner cartridge.
risks.proof: Photos showing the full machine with all parts included, including the power cord, paper tray, and any accessories.

risks.risk: The machine may be a refurbished or used unit misrepresented as new.
risks.proof: A close-up of the serial number and any wear or damage on the casing or internal components.
risks.if_unproven: priced as used, with potential for lower value

proof_requests: Close-up of the sticker with the model number, usually inside the original packaging.
Video of the machine powering on and printing a test page.
Photos of the full machine with all parts included, including power cord and paper tray.
Close-up of the serial number and any signs of wear or damage.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
